entities.summary:
The Nigerian Civil War was a pivotal, brutal conflict that ravaged Nigeria from 1967 to 1970. 

 It was a conflict that began with the secession of the eastern region and ended with the defeat of the secessionists. 

 Led by General Yakubu Gowon, the Nigerian government fought against the separatist movement led by Odumegwu Ojukwu. 

 The war resulted in the deaths of over a million people and the displacement of millions more. 

 The war also had a profound impact on the country's politics, economy, and society, and its effects can still be felt today. 

 As General Gowon himself once said, 'The Nigerian Civil War was a test of our nation's will and our ability to overcome adversity.'
